thesis_points: First publicly traded land banking REIT — 876 communities, 139,000 homesites, $8.4B homesite inventory under option

Other Agreements segment growing 3.4x from Q1–Q3 2025 — rapidly diversifying beyond Lennar's ~80% revenue share
IROIC (9.5–10.3%) exceeds WACC; value-accretive at current P/BV of ~0.87x; book value grows as inventory expands
HOPP'R technology platform (centralized land analytics + deal execution) creates a moat difficult to replicate at scale
Consensus analyst: 'Land is land — unless there's a recession, no reason to trade at a discount to book'

overview.narrative:
Tower REITs dominated today's tape, surging 1.92% on average as SBAC and CCI rallied 4.14% and 3.89% respectively, likely catching a bid from the Treasury selloff stabilizing and renewed carrier capex commentary. Hospitality and net lease posted modest gains of 0.40% and 0.30%, while healthcare was the clear laggard at -0.83%, dragged by DHC's 3.31% decline. Office remained in no-man's land at -0.09%.

The intra-sector dispersion tells the more interesting story. Within industrials, IIPR gained 2.24% while LINE dropped 1.96%—a 420bp spread suggesting idiosyncratic drivers rather than macro rotation. Tower names also showed unusual bifurcation: UNIT fell 2.52% even as the sector ripped, underscoring the fiber/small-cell vs. macro-tower divergence. Healthcare's CHCT bucking the subsector with a 1.12% gain against DHC's sharp decline highlights ongoing credit differentiation in that space.

Positioning into Friday, the tower momentum looks chaseworthy only with conviction on duration—watch the 10-year closely. We'd fade the healthcare weakness selectively; DHC looks technically oversold but fundamentally challenged. The flat retail print and narrow housing dispersion (AVB +1.26%, ELME -1.30%) suggest those sectors are coiling for a move as Q2 earnings approach. Stay nimble in rate-sensitive names ahead of next week's CPI.
